cases.description: A 'wooden, dead-eyed' performance complaint routes to higgsfield-acting and fixes eyes with a TASK, not with catchlights
cases.request: My characters look wooden and dead-eyed in every Seedance shot. How do I fix the performance?
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-acting (§ The five pillars, § Eye life) + higgsfield-seedance (the PERFORMANCE block it fills).

Wooden acting is almost always missing pressure, not missing emotion words. For each character in frame, write:

- **An objective** — a verb aimed at the partner: *make him admit he took it*.
- **Business** — a physical task the hands are doing, and the moment they stop it.
- **An eye task** — give the eyes a task aimed at the partner: *checking after each sentence whether it landed · stealing a look at the door and snapping back*. Catchlights only make that legible; they never fix a dead stare.

```
PERFORMANCE
MARA wants to make him admit he took the keys. She keeps folding the same towel while she talks; her eyes check his face after every sentence, then drop to his jacket pocket and back. When he laughs, her hands stop mid-fold — one slow blink, jaw set — and she waits.
```

cases.description: 'Generates cleanly but lands flat' routes to the scene-engine structural audit (not to prompt rewriting) and flags an inert reversal
cases.request: My heist sequence generates cleanly but lands flat and nobody can say why. Is this scene working? Outline: she cracks the safe, the alarm trips, she escapes over the roof.
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-scene-engine (§ Audit procedure) — a structural audit on text, before any more credits go into renders.

```
SCENE/SEQUENCE: the safe → alarm → roof escape

CHAIN CHECK
• Goal — get the ledger out tonight; a causal link to the story goal. Holds.
• Obstacle — the alarm jeopardizes the whole goal (global). Holds.
• Tactic — the roof is a reasonable guess, but its outcome returns no new information. Weak.
• Reversal — the alarm tripping is a turn of plot. Present.
• Value Shift — before-verdict "she is careful" → after-verdict "she is careful". No shift: INERT.

WEAKEST POINT: the reversal moves the plot but not the audience's verdict of her.

WHAT IF…
1. (Minimal) The alarm trips because she stopped to take one thing that is not the ledger — the audience re-judges her from careful to compromised.
2. (Clean) Her partner trips it deliberately; she escapes knowing it.
```
